content: The estrogen patch is a transdermal delivery system for estradiol, a form of estrogen used in hormone replacement therapy (HRT). It is primarily prescribed to alleviate menopausal symptoms such as hot flashes and vaginal dryness, as well as to prevent osteoporosis. Unlike oral estrogen tablets, the estrogen patch delivers the hormone through the skin, bypassing the liver. This method avoids the hepatic effects associated with oral estrogen and has slightly different impacts on lipid profiles, including triglycerides and cholesterol levels. The patch should be applied to areas of fatty tissue on the skin, such as the lower abdomen or buttocks. It should never be applied to the breasts. Depending on the specific brand, the patch is typically replaced either twice weekly or weekly. Some of the brand names for estrogen patches include the following: Alora® (United States) Climara® (United States) Dermestril® (United Kingdom) Elleste Solo® (United States) Esclim® (United States) Estraderm® (United Kingdom) Estradot® (United Kingdom) Evorel® (United Kingdom) Fematrix® (United Kingdom) Fempatch® (United States) FemSeven® (United Kingdom) Menostar® (United States) Vivelle-Dot® (United States) – This product was originally marketed as Vivelle® by Novartis. However, in 2000, it was replaced by a smaller version with improved adhesion, leading to the discontinuation of Vivelle® in 2003.
